raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie
raw_recipe.description: This easy smoothie is made with strawberry, banana, peanut butter, and nonfat plain yogurt for a creamy protein-packed treat with no added sugar.
raw_recipe.name: Strawberry Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie

recipeInstructions.text: Place yogurt, banana, strawberries, and peanut butter into a blender. Add ice cubes and purée until smooth.

review.reviewBody: I liked it and would make it again but I would only put in 1 T peanut butter probably because the peanut butter flavor overwhelmed it. I love peanut butter but in this I think I would prefer a banana or strawberry flavor coming out. I couldn't taste the strawberries at all so I maybe would add a few more of those also. It's definitely worth trying though.

This smoothie is really good and, with my moderations, really filling. I normally make strawberry banana smoothies but I didn't think to add peanut butter. It was a good addition. I see that a few thought it was too much peanut butter but on the contrary I think it could use a little more. I'm a peanut butter freak lol. I didn't add any sugar, the smoothie truly doesn't need any if your fruit is sweet but if you have bitter strawberries I would add a pack of stevia or something. The moderations. So, I'm vegan and do not eat yogurt so I decided to use vanilla almond milk which is delicious. I still added just one banana but I used about twelve strawberries. I then added a teaspoon of maca powder. Another trick is to nix the ice and freeze the fruit. Frozen fruit gives a nice milkshake texture and also doesn't water it down. I always use 1 1/2 cups of milk because it fills my 24oz glass mason cup and it's normally a meal replacement in the morning, sometimes for lunch as well. The recipe, as is, is a 5 and it's even better for me personally with my alterations. My take on this recipe:

1 1/2 cup almond milk
10-12 frozen strawberries
1 frozen banana
2 tablespoons peanut butter
1 tsp maca powder
I actually added five frozen strawberries instead of ones in a container and I added one freezed dried strawberry for extra flavor I loved it and I added no ice cubes
I had to substitute the plain yogurt because I didn't have any so I used Oikos triple zero peanut butter banana yogurt and it was awesome! My 9 year old even loved it!!

I agree with the other user that, personally, the peanut butter flavor over-powered the strawberry and banana. So next time I may add extra strawberries, or a second banana(I love bananas, and big smoothies). I used almond milk instead of yogurt, and since my strawberries were frozen, I added a little more than a half cup, to blend it better. I added about a tablespoon of chia seeds. Also, I used JIF natural Honey peanut butter, so it gave it a little added sweetness. Definitely will try again.

This is really really yummy. The husband and I made this last night for desert and it was delicious. We had used all of our ice when steaming broccoli for dinner, but luckily all of my strawberries and bananas were frozen, and it came out a really good consistency. Also, we only had crunchy peanut butter, but it didn't seem to make a difference - the peanuts blended up well, but I had to use a bit more pb to get the taste right (I like really peanut buttery smoothies though). Just made it again for breakfast this morning and threw in some granola - super yummy.

I loved it! I modified it a little. Used 6 frozen strawberries, non-fat vanilla yogurt(no need to sweeten), 1 banana, 4 iced cubes, 2 tbsp of peanut butter. This is comparable to smoothie king, the amount of peanut butter was just right. Idk what other people are talking about. Maybe just make a strawberry banana smoothie if the peanut butter is overwhelming, I mean it is a Strawberry banana PEANUT BUTTER smoothie.

This recipe is simple, but SO SO delicious. I rarely have fresh fruit in the house, so after the first try as written (which was great), I've been making this with: 120g frozen strawberries 175g nonfat plain yogurt 2 tbsp peanut butter I've also added 1/4 cup uncooked plain oats to help absorb some of the acidity, and that turned out fantastic. LOVE this recipe!
I changed this recipe and rated based on my own version....for 2 servings, 1 cup vanilla ice cream, 2 tbsp. peanut butter, 2 bananas, 8 strawberries...it was delicious definitely sweet enough.
I used this recipe based off of another reviewer's suggestion, and it tastes awesome (it also is a vegan recipe!): 1/2 c Chocolate soy milk (I use Silk) 1 Banana 2 tbsp Peanut Butter 10 ice cubes
Yum - I love to make this with 1/2 cup of chocolate soy milk instead of the yogurt. Chocolate peanut butter bliss.
Tried it with protein powder and almond milk. Perfecto!!!
I made this and added some milk and a few tbsps of honey. My strawberries were frozen. Delicious!
This smoothie was perfect! I added spinach, almond milk and dates. No yogurt! Very fulfilling :)
Definitely liked it but will use less peanut butter next time.
I used 1/4 cup mashed strawberries and 3 TBL PB, my favorite so far! It didn't last long enough to take a picture. Added Collagen protein for a protein-rich meal.
Made this per recipe and to me it was to chalky tasting.
Yummy I love it! I recommend this to everyone who wants to banana strawberries smoothie with

When I say I hate peanut butter plain I mean it ever since I was a kid i’ve never liked peanut butter and I’ve been trying to gain weight and have seen all these strawberry banana protein shakes so I prayed that I would like it with peanut butter and what do you know it actually tastes really good and the peanut butter makes the texture so nice and gives it such a unique flavor. So happy I tried this
I’m usually not a big peanut butter fan, but protein! This is great. Tasty and a nice blend of flavors.
